edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE; ADJUSTMENTS. The Buyer shall pay the Seller the Purchase Price for the Shares in immediately available funds at Closing. The Purchase Price shall be adjusted on a dollar-for-dollar basis as follows: (a) increased by the amount of Cash of the Company as of the Closing; (b) decreased by the amount of Indebtedness of the Company as of the Closing; (c) decreased by unpaid Transaction Expenses; and (d) increased or decreased, as applicable, by the amount by which Closing Working Capital is greater than or less than the Target Working Capital. For purposes of this Agreement: "Cash" means cash and cash equivalents determined in accordance with the Accounting Principles, net of issued but uncleared checks and restricted cash; "Indebtedness" means borrowed money, capital lease obligations, accrued interest, breakage costs, unpaid income taxes for pre-Closing periods, and similar debt-like obligations, but excluding trade payables included in Working Capital; "Transaction Expenses" means unpaid fees, costs, bonuses, change-of-control payments and expenses incurred by or on behalf of the Company or Seller in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; "Working Capital" means current assets minus current liabilities of the Company, in each case calculated in accordance with the Accounting Principles and excluding Cash, Indebtedness, Transaction Expenses and income tax assets and liabilities; "Accounting Principles" means the Company's historical accounting policies consistently applied and, to the extent not inconsistent therewith, GAAP; and "Target Working Capital" means the agreed target working capital amount set forth on Schedule 1.1. No later than five Business Days before Closing, Seller shall deliver a good-faith estimate of Cash, Indebtedness, Transaction Expenses and Closing Working Capital, together with reasonable supporting detail, and the Purchase Price paid at Closing shall be calculated using such estimate. Within ninety days after Closing, Buyer shall deliver a proposed final closing statement. Seller shall have thirty days to review such statement and reasonable access to supporting books, records and personnel. Any disputed items not resolved within thirty days after Seller's notice of dispute shall be submitted to a nationally recognized independent accounting firm mutually agreed by the parties, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator, whose determination shall be limited to the disputed items and shall be final and binding absent manifest error. The parties shall promptly pay any amounts finally determined to be owed under this Section.
edits.name: Purchase Price Adjustment Mechanism

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules, Seller represents that, to Seller's Knowledge, the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with applicable accounting principles consistently applied and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the periods indicated, subject to normal year-end adjustments, the absence of notes and the disclosures set forth in the disclosure schedules. For purposes of this Agreement, "Seller's Knowledge" means the actual knowledge of the individuals identified on Schedule 3.1, after reasonable inquiry of their direct reports with primary responsibility for the applicable subject matter.
edits.name: Financial Statement Representation

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer and its Affiliates against losses arising from breaches of Seller's representations, warranties and covenants and from liabilities of the Company to the extent arising from pre-Closing periods and not taken into account in the final purchase price adjustment; provided, however, that Seller shall have no indemnity obligation for any matter fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules, included in the final purchase price adjustment, or arising from Buyer's or the Company's post-Closing operating decisions except to the extent required by applicable law or by the terms of this Agreement. Claims for breaches of representations and warranties shall survive for eighteen months after Closing, except that fundamental representations and claims based on fraud or intentional breach shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations. Seller shall not be liable for indemnifiable losses for breaches of representations and warranties unless and until the aggregate amount of such losses exceeds the deductible basket set forth in Schedule 4.1, after which Seller shall be liable only for losses in excess of such basket. Seller's aggregate liability for breaches of representations and warranties shall not exceed the cap set forth in Schedule 4.1, except with respect to fundamental representations, fraud or intentional breach. The indemnification provisions in this Section shall be the sole and exclusive monetary remedy of the parties after Closing for matters arising under this Agreement, except for fraud, intentional breach, equitable remedies, purchase price adjustment payments and any remedies expressly provided in ancillary agreements. The party seeking indemnification shall provide prompt written notice of any claim, permit the indemnifying party to participate in and, subject to customary conflict and consent limitations, control the defense of third-party claims, and shall not settle any such claim in a manner imposing non-monetary obligations or admitting fault without the indemnifying party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
edits.name: Indemnity Limitations and Procedures
